bull.b: Sustained gross margins near 76% indicate attractive unit economics for neffy, enabling scalable contribution as volumes rise. High product-level margins provide structural support to absorb commercial spend, fund R&D or improve profitability as refill and repeat use rates mature over the next 2–6 months.

Triple-year-over-year volume growth and a 120k patient installed base reflect durable market penetration and prescriber adoption. Combined with a 148-person sales force and growing HCP repeat use, this builds a refill-driven revenue foundation and network effects that support sustainable top-line expansion.

A $201M cash position provides a meaningful runway to execute commercialization, access programs and international launches through H2 2026 and into 2027. This reduces near-term financing risk and gives management time to convert prescriptions to refills and achieve the targeted cash-flow breakeven timeline.

bear.b: Persistent, large negative operating cash flow implies ongoing reliance on cash reserves or financing to sustain commercialization. If revenue scaling or refill maturation underperforms, the company may need to raise capital, diluting shareholders or constraining strategic options, a structural risk to long-term sustainability.

Elevated SG&A tied to field expansion and DTC builds a high fixed cost base that must be covered by recurring revenue. If refill rates, payer conversions, or prescription retention lag expectations, these fixed costs will delay or impair profitability and increase the cash needed to reach breakeven.

Meaningful prior-authorization barriers and ~22–23% abandonment materially reduce conversion from written prescriptions to filled scripts. These structural access headwinds compress realized revenues (alongside ~50% gross-to-net) and slow scale-up of refill-driven revenue, raising execution risk over coming quarters.
